Linear PIZZA-23 · FR-24 · MCP game · round 2

Plugs and sockets: one shape for everything, like USB-C

Round 1 feedback (Eva): "What is this game? I know AI really well and I don't understand this simulation." Way too complex for the target persona (uses AI, wants to understand the terms). Bring back a metaphor, like the old circle-shaped and triangle-shaped holes.

What changed (3 things)

  1. The wizard is gone; the game is plugs and sockets. Your bot has a round plug. Menu has a square socket, Delivery a triangle, Bookings a round one. Tap a system to plug in: Bookings fits, the other two don't, so you tap Build an adapter · 3 wks for each. Then the Loyalty app shows up with a hexagon socket. "Every new system is a new shape. There has to be a better way." Six taps in total, every tap does one obvious thing.
  2. MCP = one socket shape everyone agreed on, like USB-C. Your bot gets the MCP plug, all four systems now show the MCP socket, each one clicks in with one tap, 0 weeks. Then a stock tracker built by strangers clicks in too. A closing picture puts the two side by side: four shapes plus adapters vs one shape for all.
  3. The term copy follows the metaphor. "Think of it as one plug shape everyone agreed on, like USB-C." No "port", no field names, no access keys, no data formats anywhere. The recap has a short aside on why people call MCP "USB-C for AI".

Open it

http://localhost:5192/game/mcp

Tap Plug in on each of the three systems, Build an adapter where it doesn't fit, tap the Loyalty app, then Show me the better way. In beat 2 tap Plug in five times (four systems, then the stock tracker), then See what this means.

Four yes/no questions

Q1 · beat 1, first screen, before you tap anything
Do you know what to do and what the shapes mean without reading twice?
Your bot card shows a round plug; each system card shows its socket shape (square, triangle, round) with a dotted outline and a "Plug in" button.
Expected yes.
Q2 · after tapping all three, and building two adapters
Does the pain read at a glance: one fits, two need adapters, weeks pile up?
Bookings green "Fits", Menu and Delivery amber "Connected through an adapter… yours to maintain", the strip says "6 wks · 2 adapters you build and maintain", then the Loyalty app arrives with yet another shape.
Expected yes.
Q3 · beat 2
After plugging everything in, could you say in one sentence what MCP solves, without reading the definition?
Something like "one plug shape everyone uses, so nothing needs an adapter". The stranger's stock tracker clicking in is the proof; the closing picture is the summary.
Expected yes. If not, tell me the sentence you would say instead.
Q4 · the metaphor
Is "USB-C" the right everyday comparison for the people we target?
It is in the term's definition and in the recap aside. The alternative is to keep only the shapes and drop the USB-C mention.
Expected yes.

Not for today

  • Shape icons are simple inline SVG; if the shapes should look more like real plugs and sockets, that is a visual pass on its own.
  • The Loyalty app never gets an adapter: it exists to show "yet another shape" and hand over to beat 2.
  • Czech copy. The game is English-only today.

How to answer

One line: 23: 1✅ 2✅ 3✅ 4✅ (or ❌ with a word on what is off).
